Choose a tuning grid

Source: vignettes/articles/tuning-grid.Rmd
tuning-grid.Rmd

Suppose you change an outcome from dollars to cents. The units and periods stay the same, but each gap between two outcomes becomes 100 times as large. The default grid still tests the same values. Use grid = "auto" to adjust the grid to the scale of the untreated outcomes.

Fit a practice panel

This example uses a panel with one treatment start date. Cross-validation compares settings on a sample of untreated cells. The example omits the bootstrap because the question here is which settings to use.

library(fasttrop)
panel <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 5,
                       n_post = 3, seed = 1)
panel$cents <- 100 * panel$y
fit <- trop(panel, "cents", "d", "unit", "time", grid = "auto",
            cv_cells = 30, se = "none", seed = 1)
fit$lambda
#>         time         unit           nn 
#>  0.500000000  0.003023458 92.061103545
fit$cv$boundary
#> NULL

fit$lambda gives the values that the search chose. If fit$cv$boundary names a parameter, the search chose a value at one end of its range. This is not proof that the fit failed. It means that the search did not compare values beyond that end.

Change the range

If the warning names the largest value of unit, add a larger value to that part of the grid. Keep the other values for comparison. The code below starts with the scaled grid and adds one candidate. Use the same seed and sample size to compare settings on the same cells.

Y <- tapply(panel$cents, list(panel$unit, panel$time), sum)
W <- tapply(panel$d, list(panel$unit, panel$time), sum)
g <- trop_grid_scaled(Y, W)
wider <- trop_grid(time = g$time, unit = c(g$unit, 2 * max(g$unit)),
                   nn = g$nn)
refit <- trop(panel, "cents", "d", "unit", "time", grid = wider,
              cv_cells = 30, se = "none", seed = 1)
rbind(first = fit$lambda, wider = refit$lambda)
#>       time        unit      nn
#> first  0.5 0.003023458 92.0611
#> wider  0.5 0.003023458 92.0611

For a warning at the smallest positive value, try a smaller positive value instead. Choose the range from the prediction errors on untreated cells, not from the size of the treatment effect.

What the scale changes

trop_grid_scaled() divides the unit values by a typical gap between untreated histories. It multiplies finite nn values by the residual scale after it removes unit and period effects. It does not change time or Inf. To inspect the two scales, use attr(g, "scales").

The scaled grid does not remove differences in level between units. If you want distances to reflect changes rather than levels, set demean = TRUE. The fit then subtracts each unit’s mean untreated outcome. When you supply a scaled grid yourself, use the same demean setting for the grid and the fit.
